reviewer: Codex storage subagent; individual current-source and all supplied current raw-flow review; no independent human approval claimed
review_status: Source/trace assessment complete; parent retains product-contract decision and active-policy ownership
common_proof: UpstreamGuard.execute invokes only its received Operation<T> at line87. AgentClient.post, available, stream and AmapGateway GET/image methods each supply their own concrete lambda. A synchronous GET capability cannot acquire the unrelated streaming lambda and its TaskService progress consumer merely because both implement Operation.run.

All 44 supplied flows were read individually. Their four sinks per primary are OutboundActorContext.register DELETE/INSERT at lines56/57 and unrelated TaskService progress writes at lines399/403. The former are not all impossible: map reads really register operations and reserve AMAP quota, as explicitly stated per finding.

Map operations have purpose=map. ExecutionGovernanceService rejects text/embedding kinds for that context; actor ID comes from the authenticated Java request, not POI/body-controlled user_id. UserQuotaService applies active-user shared-lock and per-user limits before a real supplier reservation.

These GET handlers do not change trips, plans, user permissions, feedback, exports, deletion state or payments. Bounded provider accounting is incidental to resource retrieval, not an additional user-selected business action. RFC9110 section9.2.1 explicitly permits logging/accounting side effects of safe methods.

Browser sessions are host-only HttpOnly SameSite=Strict, Secure for non-loopback. Ordinary cross-site requests do not send the authenticated cookie. Cookie-authenticated unsafe methods require the custom X-CSRF-Token guard; explicit Bearer headers are not ambient browser credentials.
limitations: Do not describe GET as having no database writes: outbound operation/audit records and AMAP quota reservations are real and may consume the documented allowance.
SameSite separates sites, not arbitrary sibling origins. This review does not authorize hostile sibling-origin hosting, permissive credentialed CORS or changing cookie domain/transport settings.

This is not a blanket CSRF suppression. Adding GET actions that change user business state, allowing model calls from map context, changing concrete callback dispatch, or changing the bound sources/flows requires new review.
Public read endpoints still need the existing anonymous/provider limits. The assessment is not proof against all service-cost or resource-exhaustion abuse.

findings.reason: Read-only POI photo/detail retrieval. The shown image-download guard to AgentClient.post is a different Operation receiver; the earlier explicit poi-detail call and actual image budget reservation can legitimately create map accounting.
The only Agent path is /capabilities/eval-policy, which forAgent explicitly excludes before any register call. The supplied synchronous callback cannot invoke streamGuarded or TaskService consumer.
The constant Agent path /capabilities/poi-search performs POI retrieval; actual map operation and AMAP quota bookkeeping are acknowledged. No trip/task/profile mutation is requested.
Delegates directly to poi with validated query/city arguments and therefore has the same read-only POI and actual map-accounting boundary.
The constant Agent path /capabilities/poi-detail returns validated public POI fields. Map operation and AMAP quota bookkeeping are real, and cannot authorize text/embedding.

Weather calls the bounded cached AmapGateway geocode/weather GET path. Its concrete callback performs HTTP GET and reserveAmap; the shown AgentClient.post receiver and stream consumer are different callbacks. Actual map accounting is acknowledged.
The constant Agent path /capabilities/rag-status is excluded by forAgent and only reads the enabled flag/model identity in the Python handler. It neither indexes nor embeds.
available uses a concrete readiness GET callback; its later /capabilities/status path is explicitly excluded from register. No streaming callback is supplied.
Only available is called. Its exact callback performs a bounded /readyz GET and updates the local availability cache; the post and stream receivers in the raw trace are not this argument.

The controller calls available and the constant /capabilities/status route. The former uses only its readiness GET callback; the latter is excluded before register and returns configuration capability flags.

Java registers this controller only for APP_ENV=validation. Python additionally requires APP_ENV=validation plus VALIDATION_ALLOW_FIXTURES=yes. The marker does not start planning/indexing; any operation record in that mode is fixture accounting.
